Using the dipole selection rules
\[\Delta l=\pm 1,\qquad \Delta m=0,\pm 1,\]
the direct transition
\[|3,0,0\rangle \to |1,0,0\rangle\]
is forbidden (since \(\Delta l=0\)). Also, \(|3,0,0\rangle\to |3,1,m\rangle\) does not contribute in the non-relativistic H-atom because the levels are degenerate, so the spontaneous E1 rate vanishes (\(\omega^3=0\)).

|3,0,0\rangle \to |2,1,-1\rangle \to |1,0,0\rangle,\quad P=\frac13,
\]

|3,0,0\rangle \to |2,1,1\rangle \to |1,0,0\rangle,\quad P=\frac13.
\]
So the total probability to reach \(|1,0,0\rangle\) via dipole cascade is

P_{\text{total}}=1.

$$|3,0,0\rangle\;\xrightarrow{E1}\;|2,1,m\rangle\;\xrightarrow{E1}\;|1,0,0\rangle,\qquad m=-1,0,1.$$ Direct $$|3,0,0\rangle\to|1,0,0\rangle$$ is dipole-forbidden \((\Delta l=0)\), so the only allowed dipole cascade is through the $$2p$$ manifold. By symmetry, the three intermediate substates are equally likely, so$$P\big(|3,0,0\rangle\to|2,1,m\rangle\to|1,0,0\rangle\big)=\frac13\quad (m=-1,0,1),$$and hence the total probability to reach $$|1,0,0\rangle$$ via dipole decay is$$P_{\text{total}}=1.$$
